A gargoyle is a grotesque statue that is attached to a building. It is carved out of stone, usually granite. It is used to get water away from the building when it rains. Gargoyles are often made to look like animals or people. The collected water comes out of their mouths. Most gargoyles were made a long time ago. People used to believe that they scared away evil spirits. Many cathedrals have many gargoyles. New buildings use rain gutters instead of gargoyles to move water. There are not many gargoyles in America. Gargoyles are often confused with grotesques. They are similar, but only gargoyles get rid of rainwater through their mouths.

Gargoyleosaurus ("gargoyle lizard") was an armoured ankylosaur which walked on four legs and had a stiff tail. It had a series of spikes running along each side of its body. Gargoyleosaurus was about 10 feet (3 m) long and was roughly 3.3 feet (1 m) tall to the top of the shoulder it may have weighed about a ton. Gargoyleosaurus is found in the of the Morrison Formation (latest Upper Jurassic) in Wyoming. It lived about 155–144 million years ago. This dinosaur had a long, narrow beak with teeth on both the upper and lower inner surface (most other ankylosaurs have teeth on only the lower beak). This plant-eater had protective body armour on the upper surface of its body and tail (hollow bony oval plates).

Garfield Ridge is one of the 77 official community areas of Chicago, Illinois, United States. It is located on the southwest side of the city. The northern half of Midway International Airport is located in this community area.

Garfield County is one of the 64 counties in the U.S. state of Colorado. As of the 2020 census, the population was 61,685. The county seat is Glenwood Springs. The county is named in honor of U.S. President James A. Garfield. Garfield County was founded on February 10, 1883.

Garfield Park is a 184 acre park in the East Garfield Park neighborhood on Chicago's West Side. It was designed as a pleasure ground by William LeBaron Jenney and is the oldest of the three large original Chicago West Side parks. It is home to the Garfield Park Conservatory, one of the largest plant conservatories in the United States. It is also the park furthest west in the Chicago park and boulevard system.

Garhajis is a clan made up of Habr Yunis and Eidagale who live in Somaliand,Ethiopia,Kenya and Djibouti. They border the habar Awal tribe to the west, the Warsangeli to the East and the reer darawiish to the southeast and ogaden to the south.

The Garibaldi Volcanic Belt is the northern part of the Cascade Volcanic Belt. It is in British Columbia and the northwestern United States. Its volcanos are the most explosive in Canada. The volcanoes are also the closest to British Columbia's densely populated southwest corner. These volcanoes are the result of subduction of the Juan de Fuca tectonic plate: the plates meet just seaward of the west coast of Vancouver Island. The volcanoes of the Garibaldi Volcanic Belt are stratovolcanoes typical of subduction zones, and include Mount Garibaldi, Mount Cayley and Mount Meager. Meager's eruption 2,350 years ago is the youngest explosive eruption in Canada. It was similar to that of Mount St. Helens in 1980 and the ongoing eruption of Montserrat in the Caribbean.
China produces more garlic than any other country in the world. About 80 percent of garlic comes from China. As of 2019, China produced 23 million tonnes of garlic every year.

Garmisch-Partenkirchen is a Landkreis (district) in Bavaria, Germany. The district is located in the Bavarian Alps and includes the highest mountain of Germany, the Zugspitze (2962 m). The district includes no towns. All places have the status of municipalities.

Garibaldi is a Mexican pop group, that wore a free version of the traditional charro costume while singing modern versions of traditional songs. Their dress and style of music caused controversy in their time. The name Garibaldi comes from Plaza Garibaldi in Mexico City where mariachi bands can be found. The group remained active from 1988 through 1994, although it continues to be active as of 2023 with new members. The group was created by Mexican TV producer Luis de Llano Macedo during the celebration of the 175 years of Mexican Independence in the musical festival held in Acapulco, Guerrero.

A garnishment is the means for collecting money judgments against a defendant by ordering third parties to pay money directly toward the plaintiff. Wage garnishments are a process of deducting money off employees' monetary compensation (including their salary); these types of garnishments continue until entire debts are paid and can be taken for any debt, however usual examples are: Wage garnishments can adversely affect credit reputation or one's ability to open bank accounts.

The Garos are a tribal people in Meghalaya, Republic of India and neighboring areas of Bangladesh, who call themselves A·chik Mande (literally "hill people," from a·chik "hill" + mande "people") or simply A·chik or Mande. They are the second-largest tribe in Meghalaya after the Khasi and comprise about a third of the local population. The Garos are one of the few remaining matrilineal societies in the world.

Garphyttan is a locality in Örebro Municipality in Örebro County in Sweden. In 2010, 1,619 people lived there. The locality is located 16 kilometers northwest of the town of Örebro. It is located near the Garphyttan National Park.

A garret is a finished, habitable attic. A gambrel roof or mansard roof is best suited to attic habitability. A garret can be an apartment, game room, etc and traditionally would have primarily held the domestic servants rooms.

Garuda Indonesia Flight 152 was a scheduled domestic Indonesian passenger flight from Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta to Polonia International Airport in Medan, North Sumatra. It was flown using an Airbus A300B4 registered PK-GAI and operated Garuda Indonesia. On September 26, 1997, Flight 152, piloted by Hance Rahmowiyogo, crashed into mountainous woodlands 30 mi from Medan during low visibility caused by the 1997 Southeast Asian haze. All 234 passengers and crew were killed in the disaster. Rahmowiyogo, age 42, had over 20 years of flying experience at Garuda Indonesia and over 12,000 flying hours. The crash site was in a ravine near the village of Buah Nabar in the Sibolangit district south of Medan. Flight 152 remains the deadliest single-plane crash in Indonesia, and the deadliest aviation accident in 1997.

Garveyism is an aspect of black nationalism that refers to the social, economic, and political policies of UNIA-ACL founder Marcus Garvey. At the movement's peak of popularity, followers of Garveyism, known as "Garveyites", numbered in the millions, with almost a thousand local divisions in the United States, the Caribbean, Central America, Canada and Africa. The ideology of Garveyism centers on the unification and empowerment of African-American men, women and children under the banner of their collective African descent, and the repatriation of African slave descendants and profits to the African continent. Garvey was fought by the African-American establishment in the U.S. An investigation by the Justice Department, directed by J. Edgar Hoover, led to Garvey's arrest on charges of mail fraud in January 1922, and his projects collapsed.
Gary Cleveland was a weightlifter from USA. Cleveland competed at the 1964 Summer Olympics. He was born on 18 January 1942 and died on 4 January 2004.

A gas syringe is a type of laboratory glassware. It is used to collect a gas or to measure the volume of a gas. Simple systems can be settled in the laboratory to collect gas or to compress it. It is usually used to explain the Ideal Gas Law.

A gas is one of the main forms, or states, of matter, like solids, liquids, and plasmas. What makes gases special is that they do not have a fixed shape or a set volume. Instead, gas particles, tiny atoms or molecules, are spread out, move freely, and have a lot of energy. Because the particles are so far apart and do not stick to each other much, gases can spread out to fill any space or container they are in. Gases can also be squeezed into smaller spaces, which is called compression. Gases are really important in science. They help us understand how heat, pressure, and motion work. Gases are all around us, from the air we breathe to the fuel in engines, and they play big roles in nature and technology. Gases have special physical properties that make them different from solids and liquids. For example, gases can be easily compressed (squeezed into a smaller space), they have low density (they are much lighter than the same volume of solid or liquid), and they can spread out and mix with other gases easily (this is called diffusion). Gases also push against the walls of whatever container they are in. This push is called pressure and comes from gas particles bouncing around and hitting the container’s walls. Scientists use a formula called the ideal gas law to describe how gases behave. It is written as PV = nRT, where: T is temperature. This formula helps predict how a gas will act if you change its temperature, pressure, or volume. But it is not perfect. Real gases do not always follow this rule, especially when they are under very high pressure or low temperature. In those cases, the gas particles get closer together and start to interact, which changes how they behave. Scientists use more detailed equations, like the van der Waals equation, to describe real gas behavior more accurately. Gases can change into other forms of matter, like liquids or solids, when the temperature or pressure changes. For example, when a gas cools down or gets squeezed tightly (compressed), it can turn into a liquid in a process called condensation. If the conditions are right, a gas can even turn directly into a solid without becoming a liquid first. This is called deposition. The opposite can also happen. If you heat a liquid, it can become a gas through vaporization (like boiling water turning into steam). And sometimes, if you heat a solid, it can turn straight into a gas without melting first. This process is called sublimation (like dry ice turning into carbon dioxide gas). These changes, called phase transitions, are very important. They happen all around us, in cloud formation, breathing, and even during volcanic eruptions. They are also used in many industries, such as refrigeration, distilling liquids, and making chemicals. Gases can be made of just one kind of element or of different elements combined. Some gases are elemental, meaning they are made of only one type of atom. Examples include hydrogen (H₂), oxygen (O₂), and the noble gases like helium and neon. Other gases are compounds, which means they are made of two or more different atoms joined together. Examples of these include carbon dioxide (CO₂), methane (CH₄), and ammonia (NH₃). Gases can also be mixtures, where many gases are blended together. A good example is air, which we breathe every day. Air is mostly made of nitrogen and oxygen, but it also contains small amounts of other gases like argon and carbon dioxide. These gas mixtures are super important. The mix of gases in Earth’s atmosphere helps regulate the planet’s temperature and makes breathing possible. In factories and hospitals, special gas mixtures are used for welding, surgery, and even to keep food fresh. Some gases belong to special groups because of how they behave or affect the world around us. Noble gases are a group of gases like helium, neon, and argon that do not easily react with other substances. This is because their atoms have a “full” outer shell of electrons, which makes them chemically stable or inert. That means they usually do not join with other atoms to form compounds. Greenhouse gases, like carbon dioxide (CO₂) and methane (CH₄), are gases that trap heat in Earth’s atmosphere. They let sunlight in but stop some of the heat from escaping, like a blanket. This helps keep the planet warm, but too much of these gases leads to global warming and climate change. There are also toxic gases, which can make people sick or be dangerous to breathe, and flammable gases, which can catch fire easily. These types of gases must be handled carefully to avoid accidents. To study and work with gases, scientists use special tools like gas chromatography and mass spectrometry. These tools help them identify what gases are present, measure how much there is, and even separate or analyze them in great detail. In a pure gas, each molecule may be made of an individual atom. It may be elemental, where each molecule is made of more than one of the same atom bound together. It may be compounds where molecules are made of many types of atoms together. An example of a monoatomic gas is neon, an example of an elemental gas is hydrogen and an example of a compound gas is carbon dioxide. A gas mixture contains a mix of any of the above types. air comprises 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, less than 1% argon, around 0.03% carbon dioxide and more other in very small quantities. Poison gases were used as chemical weapons in WWI. All gases can flow, like liquids. This means the molecules move about independently of each other. Most gases are colourless, like hydrogen. Gas particles will spread about, or diffuse, in order to fill all the space in any container such as a bottle or a room. Compared to liquids and solids, gases have a very low density and viscosity. We cannot directly see most gases since they aren't coloured. However it is possible to measure their density, volume, temperature and pressure. Pressure is the measure of how much pushing force something is putting on another object. In a gas, this is usually the gas pushing on the container of the object or, if the gas is heavy, something inside the gas. Pressure is measured in pascals. Because of Newton's third law, we can change the pressure of a gas by putting force on the object containing it. For example, squeezing a bottle with air inside pressurises the air inside. When talking about gas, pressure is often related to the container. A lot of gas in a small container would have very high pressure. A small amount of a gas in a big container would have low pressure. Gas can create pressure itself when there is a lot of it. The weight of the gas creates pressure on anything underneath it, including other gas. On a planet, this is called atmospheric pressure. The temperature of a gas is how hot or cold it is. In physics it is usually measured in Kelvin although degrees Celsius are used more elsewhere. In a gas, the average velocity, i.e. how fast they move, of the molecules is related to the temperature. The faster the gas molecules are moving, the more they collide, or smash into each other. These collisions release energy, which in a gas comes in the form of heat. Conversely if the temperature around the gas becomes hotter then the gas particles will convert the thermal energy to kinetic energy, making them move faster and making the gas hotter. A gas can go through two different state changes. If the temperature is low enough the gas can condense and turn into a liquid. Sometimes, if the temperature is low enough it can go through deposition, where it changes straight to a solid. Normally a gas must first condense to a liquid, and then freeze to become a solid, but if the temperature is very low it can skip the liquid stage and instantly become solid. Frost on the ground in winter is caused by this. Water vapour – a gas – goes into the air which is very cold, and instantly becomes ice due to deposition.

A gas station, also known as a filling station, fueling station, service station or petrol station is a facility which sells fuel and lubricants for motor vehicles. The most common fuels sold are gasoline (petrol) or diesel fuel. The fuel is dispensed by a gas pump. Some of the different kinds of fuel are Many gas stations have a convenience store close to the pumps, to make extra earnings. Some have tunnel car washs.

Gary the Snail is SpongeBob's pet snail who lives with him in their pineapple house. He meows and acts like a cat. He cannot talk but SpongeBob can understand him. Gary is usually shown to be very smart. Gary the Snail is voiced by Tom Kenny.

A gas balloon is a kind of balloon that uses a gas of low density to fly using buoyancy. Gas balloons sometimes fly very high, very far, and for a very long time. A gas balloon is different from a hot air balloon. A hot air balloon uses a fire to lower the density of air. A gas balloon does not use fire. The most common use for gas balloons are to measure the atmosphere. These are called weather balloons. Some gas balloons carry people.

Gas chromatography (GC) is a type of chromatography that scientists use to separate and study substances that can turn into gas without breaking apart. It is often used to check how pure a substance is or to separate the parts of a mixture to see what’s inside. It is one of the most common and useful methods in analytical chemistry because it is very fast, sensitive, and accurate. In gas chromatography, the sample is first vaporized, which means it is turned into a gas. Then, an inert gas like helium or nitrogen carries the sample through a long tube called a column. Inside the column, there is a special coating called the stationary phase. As the different parts of the sample move through the column, they stick to the coating in different ways. Some parts move faster, and some move slower. Because of this, the parts get separated by the time they come out of the column. A detector at the end then finds and records each part, allowing scientists to know what’s in the sample and how much of it there is. Gas chromatography is used in many industries and science fields, like medicine, environment testing, food safety, fuel research, and crime investigations. It works best on organic compounds that can turn into gas and would not break down from heat. Some common uses include finding pesticides in food, checking for pollution in the air, measuring alcohol levels in blood, studying perfumes and essential oils, and testing how pure a chemical is Because gas chromatography can find even tiny amounts of substances very accurately, it is very important for quality control and following safety rules in labs and industries. A gas chromatograph is a machine made up of several important parts. These include a sample injection port, where the sample is added; a column, which can be packed or very thin like a capillary tube; an oven that controls the temperature; and a detector that finds and measures the substances coming out of the column. Two common types of detectors are the flame ionization detector (FID) and the thermal conductivity detector (TCD). The FID is very good at finding hydrocarbons, which are found in fuels and many organic compounds. The TCD can detect most gases and is used for general purposes. Some gas chromatography systems include mass spectrometry (GC-MS). This setup not only separates the different parts of a mixture but also helps identify exactly what each part is. Because of its powerful abilities, GC-MS is used often in forensic labs and environmental testing. Gas chromatography can be done in different ways. In isothermal runs, the oven stays at the same temperature the whole time. In temperature-programmed runs, the oven slowly gets hotter during the test. This helps separate substances that have different boiling points more clearly. Sometimes, scientists use a special process called derivatization. This changes substances that do not easily turn into gas, or are too polar, so they can be tested with gas chromatography. This lets scientists study an even wider range of chemicals. Gas chromatography (GC) has many advantages, but it also has some limits. It only works well with substances that can be turned into gas without breaking apart. If a substance is too sensitive to heat or does not evaporate easily, then GC would not work well for it. In those cases, scientists use other methods, like liquid chromatography (LC), which is better for studying these types of substances. Even with its limits, GC is still a very important tool in science. New improvements in equipment, column design, and computer software keep making it better and more powerful for analyzing all kinds of mixtures. In selecting a carrier gas it is important to select a gas that will not react with the components of the sample. The carrier gas should also be able to withstand high temperatures due to the oven. The flow rate of the carrier gas is important in that if it is too high there is not enough time for the sample to interact with the column and no separation will be seen, if it is too slow the experiment may take a very long time. The main type of columns used in gas chromatography is a capillary column. Packed columns are created of fused silica or stainless steel. To increase separation of a gas sample columns must be created of a large length and are coiled to fit inside of the oven. Capillary columns are separated into two categories; wall coated open tubular and support coated open tubular. WCOT are capillary tubes with a thin layer of stationary phase, and in SCOT, the tube is lined with a thin film of support material. As the sample moves through the column the individual parts of the sample become contained with the material inside of the column and are then released. This action allows for a sample to become separated. It is important that the oven is capable of maintaining a constant temperature. Since movement of the sample through the column relies on the boiling point of the sample being analyzed, the oven should be set to a temperature that is slightly higher than its boiling point. For samples with a large boiling range, a temperature program can be used, in which the column temperature is raised. By using a high temperature, the sample moves through the column faster, while at lower temperatures the sample moves slower, but better resolution is achieved. Many types of detectors are used in gas chromatographic separations, with the most common are flame ionization, thermal conductivity, and mass spectrometry detectors. In a flame ionization detectors, the separated sample from the column is directed into a flame. By creating a voltage near the burner tip and the detector, the ions that are produced from the flame travel towards the detector. Flame detectors are not capable of detecting H2O, CO2, SO2, and CO. With a thermal conductivity detector, the sample from the column is passed into an area that is electrically heated. The thermal conductivity of the column is reduced when the sample passes over by. When this occurs the detector heats up and measures the change in resistance. The thermal conductivity detector is capable of detecting all types of compounds. A mass spectrometer measures the mass to charge ratio of fragmented ions of a sample. The output of a column can be feed directly into the ionization chamber of the mass spectrometer. A mass spectrometry detector is capable of being able to obtain information from incompletely separated components. Two types of mass spectrometer detectors used are quadrupole and time of flight mass analyzers. In a quadrupole detector, a voltage is produced which makes ions of a specific mass to travel to the detector. In a time of flight mass analyzer, the speed of an ion is measured allowing the mass to charge ratio to be known. Gas chromatography is regularly used to describe what is inside a complex sample. The information obtained from gas chromatography is placed into a graph of detector response versus the time the sample leaves the column. If the separate parts of a complex sample come out at different times far apart from one another it is possible to determine what came out of the column. If a sample is compared to a standard calibration it is possible to know how much of a separated part of the sample makes up the sample. This is useful in monitoring quality of a product such as medicine, beverage, or perfume.

A discharge tube, or a gas-filled tube is an arrangement of electrodes in an insulated container, containing a gas. Very often, glass or ceramics are used as insulation. When there is enough charge on these electrodes, there will be an electric discharge, which will produce light. In the 19th century, Heinrich Geißler developed the Geissler tube,and Philipp Lenard did experiments that led to the development of the vacuum pump. Both technologies were used to develop the discharge tube. The most common kind of discharge tube is the gas discharge lamp.

Exchange of gases or gas exchange is carried out by organisms. Animals breathe out carbon dioxide and breathe in oxygen. Plants use carbon dioxide to carry out photosynthesis, making oxygen. Plants only do this when there is light. Plants breathe day and night. In the human respiratory system, gas exchange happens in the alveolus (alveoli for plural). These are in the lungs and help with diffusion. Oxygen diffuses into the bloodstream, from the air. Oxygen is used in aerobic respiration. Carbon dioxide diffuses out of the bloodstream, into the air. Carbon dioxide is a waste product made by respiration. In eukaryotes, respiration is carried out by the mitochondria. However, in some cells it is carried out by the cytoplasm. For more information visit cellular respiration.

Gas discharge lamps are a family of artificial light sources (or lamps). These lamps produce light by sending electricity through an ionized gas. Most of these lamps use a noble gas (often argon or neon gas), or a combination of noble gases, but they often contain other materials, such as mercury, sodium or metal halides. The gases in these lamps are ionized in operation. This means that there are free electrons. When an electric current is sent through the gas, electrons collide with atoms of the gas and the metals. This will mean that some reach a higher energy state. When they fall back into the lower energy state, they will emit the energy in the form of light. The fluorescent lamp is probably the best known gas discharge lamp. Sodium vapor lamps are commonplace as streetlights. Neon lamps are used in advertising. Gas-discharge lamps have a long life and a high efficiency, but they are more complicated to manufacture, which makes them more expensive to buy than incandescent lamps. Due to their greater efficiency, gas-discharge lamps replaced incandescent light bulbs for many purposes in the late 20th century. Early in the 21st century, light-emitting diodes improved, with even higher efficiency. They began to replace some gas discharge lamps.

A gas heater is a heater used to heat a room or outside area by burning natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas, propane, or butane. A gas heater controls its cycle by using a mechanical or electronic thermostat. Gas flow is turned on with a valve. The gas is lit by an electric filament or pilot light. Flames heat a radiator in the air duct, convection or a fan may distribute the heat to the room. Non-flued heaters – also known as unvented heaters, vent-free heaters, or flueless fires, are either permanently installed or can be moved around, and sometimes will have a catalytic converter. Non-flued heaters can be not safe if safety rules are not followed. There must be enough ventilation and they must be kept clean. They should always be switched off before sleeping. If they are operating correctly then the main emissions of a non-flued gas heater are water vapor, carbon dioxide, and nitrogen dioxide. Flued heaters are permanently installed wherever they are placed. The flue, if properly installed correctly should remove all of the heater emissions. A correctly operating flued gas heater is safe for use. Not all flued heaters are allowed for use in indoor living spaces. Some flued gas heaters can be used indoors, but not where people eat or sleep. For example, the normal power-vented garage unit heater in North America. These heaters are best in garages, commercial areas, or industrial spaces. They are not good where people live.

Gasoline, or petrol, is a toxic, flammable and clear liquid that is mostly used as a fuel in internal combustion engines. More precisely, used as a fuel for spark-ignited internal combustion engines. It is made by boiling petroleum, a fossil fuel. In a distillation process, petroleum is heated to a very high temperature, then it separates into its components, one of them is gasoline. This is an expensive process. It is made mostly of octane (C8H18), a hydrocarbon. Gasoline is sold at gas stations (petrol stations). In order to burn properly in high-compression internal combustion engines, each brand of gasoline includes gasoline additives. So, the exact make up of gasoline is different at different stations. Gasoline is graded by its octane rating that measures how well it will burn. Most car engines can burn "regular" gasoline which has an octane rating of 87. Precision-made engines require or prefer "premium" gasoline with an octane rating of 93. Most stations offer three different mixtures of gasoline with three separate octane ratings and prices. Gasoline is most often used in vehicles like cars, vans, etc. Gasoline can be used in a wide variety of other things that we use every day, such as lawnmowers, leaf blowers, and small boat motors. Some larger vehicles like trucks or ships may use diesel fuel instead of gasoline. Gasoline is very dangerous. It can explode when an electric spark lights it. It is also harmful if a human drinks it or if it gets on the skin. It hurts the environment and human health by creating poisonous gases such as carbon monoxide. If a gasoline engine is used indoors or in a closed space, the carbon monoxide can cause death in minutes. Many people die every year from using gasoline-powered generators indoors, or leaving vehicles running inside a garage. The US accounts for about 44% of the world’s gasoline consumption. In 2003 The US consumed 476.474 GL, which equates to 1.3 gigalitres of gasoline each day (about 360 million US or 300 million imperial gallons). The US used about 510 billion litres (138 billion US gal/115 billion imp gal) of gasoline in 2006, of which 5.6% was mid-grade and 9.5% was premium grade. Unlike the US, countries in Europe impose substantial taxes on fuels such as gasoline. For example, price for gasoline in Europe is more than twice that in the US. Because of the low fuel taxes, the retail price of gasoline in the US is subject to greater changes (than outside the US) when calculated as a percentage of cost-per-unit. From 1998 to 2004, the price of gasoline was between $1 and $2 USD per U.S. gallon. After 2004, the price increased until the average gas price reached a high of $4.11 per U.S. gallon in mid-2008, then dropped approximately $2.60 per U.S. gallon as of September 2009. Recently, the U.S. has experienced an upswing in gas prices of 13.51% from Jan 31st to March 7, 2011. Most consumer goods have posted prices that exclude tax; taxes are added based on a percentage of the purchase price. Because of primitive gasoline pumps in the 1920s, United States gasoline prices are posted with taxes included and the taxes are set on cents per gallon. Taxes are added by federal, state and local governments. (These taxes collect the cost of maintaining the roads.) As of 2009, the federal tax is 18.4¢ per gallon for gasoline and 24.4¢ per gallon for diesel (excluding red diesel). Among states, the highest gasoline tax rates, as of January 2011, are California (47.7¢/gal), New York (47.3¢/gal), Hawaii (45.8¢/gal), and Connecticut (45.2¢/gal). The federal government and many states fail to increase their gasoline taxes over time with inflation. However, some states also charge a sales tax as a percentage and vary in amount depending on the cost of the gasoline. About 9% of all gasoline sold in the US in May 2009 was premium grade, according to the Energy Information Administration. Some car manufacturers "recommend" premium gasoline but have computer-controlled engines that adjust the timing to avoid knocking. So, most cars can burn regular grade gasoline but at a slightly reduced performance. The Associated Press said premium gas–which is a higher octane and costs several cents a gallon more than regular unleaded–should be used only if the manufacturer says it is “required”. To reduce the use of imported oil, the US uses Gasohol (10% ethanol) and E85 (85% ethanol) ethanol/gasoline mixtures. Brazil has the largest national fuel ethanol industry. Gasoline sold in Brazil contains at least 25% anhydrous ethanol. Hydrous ethanol (about 95% ethanol and 5% water) can be used as fuel in more than 90% of new cars sold in the country. Brazilian ethanol is produced from sugar cane and noted for high carbon sequestration.

Gaslighting is slang for "making someone question their own reality". A "gaslighter" is a person who uses words and sometimes tricks to make others unsure of what is real and what is not real. This can be very upsetting. Gaslighting is only possible when the victim is a vulnerable person - for example, when the gaslighter is a powerful person, or if the victim fears that not believing the gaslighter will bring them grief. Sometimes, people don't know they are gaslighting others. The term "gaslighting" comes from a play that was first performed in 1938 and made into a movie in 1944. The movie was called Gaslight, and it was a story about a husband who tries to make his wife believe that she is going crazy by constantly dimming the gas lights in their home, while telling her that they were just as bright as usual. Nowadays gaslighting is used to describe a type of psychological abuse where the abuser makes their victim doubt their own sanity. This manipulative abuse ranges from subtle tactics such as contradicting everything the victim says, to more aggressive tactics like outright lies. The result is a total destruction of the victim's trust in their own ability to recognise reality.

Gasherbrum I is a 8080 m mountain in the Karakoram range, in China and Pakistan. It is also known as K5 and Hidden Peak. It is the 11th highest mountain in the world. The first people to reach the top were Pete Schoening and Andy Kauffman in 1958.

Gasherbrum II is a 8035 m mountain in the Karakoram range, in China and Pakistan. It is also known as K4. It is the 13th highest mountain in the world. The first people to reach the top were Fritz Moravec, Josef Larch, and Hans Willenpart, in 1956.

Gasherbrum III is a 7952 m mountain in the Karakoram range, in China and Pakistan. It is also known as K3a. It is the 15th highest mountain in the world. The first people to reach the top were Wanda Rutkiewicz, Alison Chadwick-Onyszkiewicz, Janusz Onyszkiewicz and Krzysztof Zdzitowiecki, in 1975. As of 2018, only two expeditions ever made it to the top.

Gasherbrum IV is a 7925 m mountain in the Karakoram range, in China and Pakistan. It is also known as K3. It is the 17th highest mountain in the world. A well known feature is the west face, which is called the Shining Wall. Gasherbrum IV is considered as one of the most difficult mountains to climb. The first people to reach the top were Walter Bonatti and Carlo Mauri, in 1958.

Gasherbrum V is a 7133 m mountain in the Karakoram range, in Pakistan. It was thought to be part of Gasherbrum IV until 1934. The first people to reach the top were Seong Nak-jong and Ahn Chi-young, in 2014.
Gasoline additives increase gasoline's octane rating or act as corrosion inhibitors or lubricants, thus allowing the use of higher compression ratios for greater efficiency and power.

Gasterosteoidei is a suborder of ray-finned fishes that includes the sticklebacks and relatives. It is currently classified in the order Scorpaeniformes. Gasterosteoidei is treated as a suborder within the order Scorpaeniformes in the 5th edition of Fishes of the World, but in other classifications it is treated as the infraorder Gasterosteales. Historically, Gasterosteoidei was called the Gasterosteiformes. Recent studies show that the more typical members of that group (like scorpionfishes) arecloser to the "true" Gasterosteiformes, so we can see why it was changed. Family Hypoptychidae Steindachner, 1880 (Korean sandlance) Family Aulorhynchidae Gill, 1861 (Tubesnouts) Family Gasterosteidae Bonaparte, 1831 (Sticklebacks) Family Indostomidae Prashad & Mukerji, 1929 (Armoured sticklebacks) These fish have the possession of an upper jaw and a well developed upward pointing process on the premaxilla. They have small mouths. The body usually has dermal plates. Here are two of the extinct genera of the Gasterosteoidei:

Gasterosteus is a genus of ray-finned fishes belonging to the family Gasterosteidae in the suborder Gasterosteoidei. These fishes are found in freshwater, brackish water and marine habitats in the Holarctic region. Gastrioceratoidea is one of 17 superfamilies of the Goniatitina suborder. They are an extinct group of ammonoid, which are similar to squids and cuttlefish.

Gastritis is an inflammation of the lining of the stomach. It has many possible causes. The main causes are drinking too much alcohol, or using nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (also known as NSAIDs) such as aspirin or ibuprofen for too long. Sometimes gastritis starts after major surgery, serious injury, burns, or infections. People who have had weight loss surgery may also get gastritis. Long term causes are infection with bacteria, mainly Helicobacter pylori. Certain diseases, such as pernicious anemia, chronic bile reflux, stress and certain autoimmune disorders can cause gastritis as well. The most common symptom is abdominal pain. Other symptoms are indigestion, abdominal bloating, nausea, and vomiting. Some may have a feeling of fullness or burning in the upper abdomen. A gastroscopy, blood test, complete blood count test, or a faeces test may be used to diagnose gastritis. Treatment includes taking antacids or other medicines, such as proton pump inhibitors or antibiotics, and avoiding hot or spicy foods. For those with pernicious anemia, B12 injections are given.

Gastralia are bones protecting the ventral area of a vertebrate. They are found in some living and fossil reptiles. Crocodiles, plesiosaurs, ichthyosaurs, and theropod dinosaurs have gastralia. Unlike ribs, they are not connected to the vertebrae.

Gastrointestinal bleeding (GI bleed), also known as gastrointestinal hemorrhage, is all forms of bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, from the mouth to the rectum. When there is significant blood loss over a short time, symptoms may include vomiting red blood, vomiting black blood, bloody stool, or black stool. Small amounts of bleeding over a long time may cause iron-deficiency anemia resulting in feeling tired or heart-related chest pain. Other symptoms may include abdominal pain, shortness of breath, pale skin, or passing out. Sometimes in those with small amounts of bleeding no symptoms may be present.

Gastrointestinal diseases are about diseases that affect the gastrointestinal tract. They include the oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, the liver, gallbladder, and pancreas.

The long-footed marsupial frog, Pastaza marsupial frog or rana marsupial de pies largos (Gastrotheca longipes) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador and Peru. This frog has a large, strong body. The adult male frog is 61.2–70.8 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 70.0–88.3 mm. The skin of the frog's back and sides is green with some white marks. Some frogs have brown or white color near the eyes and jaw. The upper lip of the mouth is white and the lower lip is green. The legs are green with white marks. The bottoms of the feet are green in color. The frog's leg bones are green in color too. The knees have brown marks on them. The throat and chest are cream-yellow in color. The belly is cream-white or green with cream-white marks. The iris of the eye is white with brown lines. Scientists gave this frog the Latin name longipes from longus for "long" and pes for "feet." This frog lives in the treetops. People see them at night on bushes and trees. It does not live in places that human beings have changed. Scientists have seen the frog between 185 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places: Santiago-Comaina Reserved Zone of Peru and Ecuador, Tiputini Biodiversity Station, and Yasuní National Park. The female frog carries the egg in a bag of skin on her back. Scientists have seen 15-17 eggs in a female's bag at a time. The eggs are big for frog eggs, 10.9 mm across. Scientists say that this frog has fewer, bigger eggs than other frogs, because it hatches as a small froglet and not a swimming tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frogs are not in danger of dying out. In some places, people change the places where the frogs live to get wood to use and make farms. Scientists are not sure whether the disease chytridiomycosis can hurt this frog.

The lower-toothed marsupial frog, detente marsupial frog, Gunther's marsupial frog, or rana marsupial dentata (Gastrotheca guentheri) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador and Colombia. This frog has a large, strong body. The adult make frog is 67.8–76.0 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 69.9–82.0 mm. The skin of the frog's back is brown with red marks or dark brown makrs or it is dark brown to gray-black with light marks or it is brown with black or green marks. Some frogs have yellow-green color near the eyes. The sides of the body are dark brown, yellow-brown, or pink in color and some frogs have cream-white or dark brown marks. The legs have dark lines going across. The throat and chest are gray-green or brown in color. The belly is brown, gray-brown, gray-green, or green-white in color. The toes are olive green in color. The tongue is bright orange or yellow in color. The iris of the eye is pearly in color on top with dark brown triangles and pink or brown-pink in color. Scientists gave this frog the Latin name for Albert C. L. G. Günther of the British Museum of Natural History. This frog is awake at night and lives in trees. It lives in the bromeliad plants that grow high in the trees. Scientists sometimes see this frog in forests that are growing back. Scientists have seen the frog between 1200 and above sea level. Scientists have saw the frog in Parque Nacional Natural Munchique and near Reserva Ecológica Los Illinizas. The female frog carries the egg in a bag of skin on her back. Scientists have seen 12-15 eggs in a female's bag at a time. This frog hatches out of its egg as a small froglet and not a swimming tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say they do not know if this frog is in danger of dying out. In some places, people change the places where the frogs live to get wood to use, make farms, raise animals, and make places to live. Scientists think climate change could hurt this frog too.

The thin-snouted marsupial frog, Pacific marsupial frog, or rana marsupial de nariz estrecha, (Gastrotheca angustifrons) is a frog. It lives in Colombia and Ecuador. The adult male frog is 56.5-73.2 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 63.5-91.8 mm. The skin of the frog's back is brown, olive-brown, or yellow-brown in color. The belly is white. Some frogs have dark brown marks on their bellies and some do not. There is a white or light yellow mark below the eye. The iris of the eye is light bronze or light olive in color. Scientists gave this frog the Latin name angustus meaning "stretched" and fros meaning "front." This frog lives in trees. People see it on plants in forests with water in the air. People see it on bushes near streams in forests. Scientists have seen the frog between 100 andabove sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in very big danger of dying out. People change the places where the frogs live. People cut down trees to get wood to use, dig in the ground for good rocks, make farms even though it is against the law to make farms in this place. People also put chemicals on these farms, and these chemicals can hurt the frog. Scientists also think disease could have killed many frogs, but they are not sure.

The Popayan marsupial frog (Gastrotheca argenteovirens) is a frog. It lives in Colombia. This frog lives in cloud forest, subparamo, and on farms. People see it near streams in forests. Scientists have seen the frog between 1760 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She carries the tadpoles to water. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out.

The Igaracu marsupial frog (Gastrotheca fissipes) is a frog. It lives in Brazil. This frog lives in forest that was never cut down and forest that is growing back. People see the frog near bromeliad plants that grow on the ground and bromeliad plants that grow on trees. The young froglets grow in these plants. Scientists have seen the frog between 0 andabove sea level. Scientists have seen this frog in protected places. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frog lives to make farms, tree farms, places for cows to eat grass, and towns. People also pick bromeliad plants because they are beautiful, which can hurt the frog.

The horned marsupial frog or rana marsupial con cuernos (Gastrotheca cornuta) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador, Panama, Costa Rica, and Colombia. The adult male frog is 66 to 81 mm long from nose to rear end. The adult female frog is 77 mm. There are 8-12 ridges on the body going across. There are triangles of skin on top of the eyes that look like horns. The skin of the frog's back is dark brown during the day and light brown at night. There is a dark brown stripe from the eardrum to where the legs meet the body. The belly is pink to light brown in color. The throat is brown in color. The iris of the eye is bronze on the outside and cream-yellow or olive green in the middle. This frog lives high in trees where the branches come together like a roof. It lives in both forest that was never cut down and forest that is growing back as long as there is enough water in the air, but it does not live anywhere that is not a forest. Scientists have seen the frog between 0 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frogs near Parque Nacional Katios. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Even when the animal is still in its egg, it does not look like a tadpole. For example, many species of frog have keratin in their mouths like tadpoles do before they hatch out of their eggs, but G. cornuta does not. This frog has the biggest eggs of any amphibian. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in very big danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frog lives to make farms, even where this is against the law, to get wood to use, and to make places for people to live. The chemicals people use on farms can also hurt the frog. Scientists saw that many of the frogs died at the same time. They think the fungal disease chytridiomycosis could have killed the frogs, that climate change could have killed the frogs, or both, but they are not sure. Scientists from the Panama Amphibian Rescue and Conservation Project in Panama and from Balsa de los Sapos in Ecuador have some of the frogs. These frogs have young, so the frog is less likely to die out.

The tiny-fingered marsupial frog (Gastrotheca microdiscus) is a frog. It lives in Brazil. This frog lives high in the trees where the branches come together like a roof. It only lives in forests that have never been cut down. The frogs live in and near bromeliad plants. Scientists have seen the frog between 800 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The eggs hatch into small froglets. The froglets live in bromeliad plants. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. Scientists think the frog could be in some danger when people change the places where the frog lives to make farms, tree farms, and places for cows to eat grass. Sometimes people come into the forest to take the bromeliad plants because they are beautiful.

The Lojana marsupial frog (Gastrotheca lojana) is a frog. It lives in Brazil. The adult male frog is about 40.2–61.0 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is about 54.1–76.1 mm. The skin of the frog's back is light yellow, brown, or green in color with a light brown or bronze line down the side of the body, with or without yellow-green marks. The sides of the body are dark brown, or light-brown-bronze in color with or without some dark blue-gray color. Some frogs have more blue-gray color than other frogs do. The belly is dark brown and white in color. The iris of the eye is bronze in color. Scientists named this frog for where they found it: The province Loja. This frog lives in cloud forest and in places with small, woody plants. During the day, people see them on agave plants and under rocks. At night, they see these frogs on other plants. Scientists have seen the frog between 1700 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She puts the tadpoles in small pools of water and in streams with still places. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in some danger of dying out. People put bad chemicals in the water. The frog is also in danger when people change the places where the frog lives to make towns, tree farms, and places for animals to eat grass. Scientists also found the dangerous fungus Batrachocytrium dendrobatidis can kill the frog, but they do not think it kills many. Cats and chickens can also kill some frogs.

The white-lined tree frog (Gastrotheca albolineata) is a frog. It lives in Brazil. This frog lives in trees where the branches come together like a roof on plants. This frog needs tall trees: It can live in the forest that has never been cut down and forest that has been growing back for a long time. Scientists have seen the frog between 600 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places. The female frog carries her eggs on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. Years ago, people cut down many trees in the Atlantic forest. There are still many trees left in protected parks and in steep places where people could not cut them. In some places, the frogs are in some danger when people change the places where the frog lives to make towns, farms, tree farms, and places to raise animals.

Helena's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca helenae) is a frog. It lives in Peru. This frog is awake at night. It lives in paramo grassy plces and sometimes cloud forests. People see the frog on bromeliad plants, moss, and rotten wood. Scientists have seen the frog between 2300 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in a protected place: Parque Nacional Natural Tamá. The female frog carries her eggs on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in danger of dying out. Before people made the Parque Nacional Natural Tamá, people turned El Tamá Páramo into places to raise cows, which meant the frogs could not live there any more. Now that the park is a park, the grasslands are slowly growing back. Outside the park, the frog is in danger from fires, people cutting down trees to get wood, and people raising animals. This frog is very sensitive. Even small changes in the places where it lives can hurt it. So far, scientists have not found the dangerous fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis on this frog.

Griswold's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca griswoldi) is a frog. It lives in Peru. This frog lives on the ground in dry puna grassy places and places with small, woody plants. People have also seen this frog on some farms. People see frogs underneath stones and in places with water. Scientists have seen the frog between 3000 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in a protected place: Pui Pui Protection Forest. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. People have seen this frog on some farms.

The gold-spotted marsupial frog (Gastrotheca aureomaculata) is a frog. It lives in Colombia. This frog lives in trees. People see it on plants next to streams in forests on the Andes mountains. Sometimes people see it on garden trees or in bushes. Scientists have seen the frog between 2000 and above sea level. Scientists have not seen the frog in a protected place, Parque Nacional Natural Puracé. It also lives on land that belongs to the Naza and Paez people, who do not allow farmers to change the land. This is good for the frogs. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She brings the tadpoles to small pools with grass in them that dry up for part of the year. Scientists have seen female frogs with as many as 116 eggs in their bags at a time. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives to get wood to use and make farms, even where that is against the law.

The Abra Acanacu marsupial frog (Gastrotheca excubitor) is a frog. It lives in Peru. This frog lives on the ground in puna with mosses. It lives high in the hills where trees do not grow. Sometimes people see it on farms. Scientists have seen the frog between 3080 and above sea level. Scientists have seen this frog in protected places: Manu National Park, Machu Picchu Historical Sanctuary, ACP Abra Málaga, and ACP Ukumari Llakta. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. Each female has about 20 eggs at a time. The eggs are about 6 mm long. The young come out as small frogs, not tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in some danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives to make farms, for example tea and coffee farms, and things for visitors. Scientists found the dangerous fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis on some of these frogs, but the disease chytridiomycosis does not always kill it. This is because germs on the frog's skin kill the fungus and protect the frog.

The Antioquia marsupial frog (Gastrotheca bufona) is a frog. It lives in Colombia. This frog lives high in the trees in forest that has never been cut down. Scientists have seen the frog between 1700 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as small frogs, not tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in some danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives to make farms and places for animals and to get wood to use.

Dunn's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca dunni) is a frog. It lives in Colombia. This frog lives in forests that were never cut down and forests that are growing back and in grassy places. People have also seen it on farms and gardens in towns, so long as there is water for its young. Scientists have seen the frog between 2000 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She brings the tadpoles to water. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out.

The Salta marsupial frog or Baritú’s marsupial frog (Gastrotheca chrysosticta) is a frog. It lives in Argentina. Scientists think it could also live in Bolivia. This frog lives high in the trees, in holes in trees, and in bromeliad plants that grow on trees. It lives in Yungas forests in the Andes Mountains. Scientists have seen the frog between 600 and above sea level. Scientists have seen this frog a protected place: Baritú National Park. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The female brings the tadpoles to water on the ground in the forest. The tadpoles grow into frogs there. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in danger of dying out. People let cows go into Baritú National Park. People change the places where the frog lives by cutting down trees to get wood to sell, raise cows, and make things people need to move around.

La Banderita marsupial frog (Gastrotheca gracilis) is a frog. It lives in Argentina. This frog lives in treetops, holes in trees, and in cracks in rocks in Yungas forests and grasslands in the Andes Mountains. People have also seen the frog near roads and in Yungas forests that were cut down or burned but are growing back. Scientists have seen the frog between 1400 and above sea level. Scientists have seen this frog in protected places: Campo de los Alisos National Park and Los Sosa Provincial Reserve. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The eggs hatch into tadpoles in the bag. The female frog carries the tadpoles to water, where they become frogs. Scientists from the IUCN and Argentina say the frog is in danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives by cutting down too many trees. Wildfires can also change the frog's home too much for the frog to live there. In 2014, many pigs were in Los Sosa Provincial Reserve and killed many tadpoles there.

The helmeted marsupial frog (Gastrotheca galeata) is a frog. It lives in Peru. This frog has heavy bones in its head and legs, and almost no webbed skin on the feet, so scientists think the frog might dig in the ground. This frog lives in cloud forests, dry forests, places where animals eat grass, and other places. During the day, people see the frogs in cracks in logs and in the ground, and under rocks. At night, they see it on branches. Scientists have seen the frog between 1740 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as small froglets, not tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say the they do not know if the frog is in danger of dying out. They think farms could affect the frog.

The Andaqui marsupial frog, Andes marsupial frog, or rana marsupial Andaquí (Gastrotheca andaquiensis) is a frog. It lives in Colombia and Ecuador. This frog can be as big as 77 mm long from nose to rear end. This frog does not have bony skin on its head. The male frogs and female frogs are different colors. The male frogs are brown and the female frogs are green. Some frogs have red spots and others do not. Some scientists saw that the inside of the frog's mouth was blue. Scientists named the frog for the Andaquíes people who live near where they first found the frog. This frog lives in trees. People see this frog on plants near water in cloud forests. Scientists are not sure if it can live in other places, for example forests that are growing back. Scientists have seen the frog between 1000 and above sea level. There are protected places where the frog lives: Reserva Ecológica Cayambe-Coca, Reserva Ecológica Antisana, Parque Nacional Sumaco Napo-Galeras, Parque Nacional Llanganates, Parque Nacional Sangay, and Parque Nacional Natural Cueva de los Guacheros. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as small froglets, not tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say this frog is not in danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives to get wood to use, make small farms, and make small places to raise animals.

The Rio Calima marsupial frog, arboreal marsupial frog, or rana marsupial Arbórea (Gastrotheca dendronastes) is a frog. It lives in Colombia and Ecuador. The adult male frog is about 39.8–74.8 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is about 61.9–73.5 mm long. This frog is different colors during the day and at night. At night, the skin of the frog's back is brown with darker brown stripes across. During the day, the skin of the frog's back is lighter brown or olive-brown in color with pink stripes going across and green marks. The sides of the body can be olive-green or dark brown in color with cream-white stripes. There is a cream-white line on the lip. The skin between the toes is red-brown in color. The belly is cream-yellow in color with red-brown marks. The iris of the eye is bronze in color with small black lines. This frog lives on plants in forests that have never been cut down and forests that are growing back. People see them in ravines that have streams in them. People see them on branches or Heliconia 2 to above the ground. Scientists have seen the frog between 1230 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places, for example Parque Nacional Natural Farallones de Cali. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as small froglets, not tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say this frog is in danger of dying out. Scientists think there are no more than 249 adult frogs alive at any one time. People change the places where the frog lives to make farms, make places for cows, and dig in the ground. Many of the frogs died in the 1990s. Scientists think it could have been disease but they are not sure.

The Busa marsupial frog, Azuay marsupial frog, or rana marsupial de Busa (Gastrotheca litonedis) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador. The adult male frog is about 48.9–57.4 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is about 53.5–62.4 mm long. The skin of the frog's back is either all green or all brown in color. Some frogs have dark brown marks on their backs. The sides of the body are bronze-brown in color. The places where the four legs meet the body are light blue in color. The belly is cream-gray in color. The iris of the eye is deep brown in color with brown lines in it. Scientists named this frog litonedis for the Greek word litos for "flat" and nedys for "belly." This frog is awake at night. It lives in and out of trees. It can live in forests and in other places. Scientists have seen the frog between 2750 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She brings the tadpoles to water that does not move. Scientists from the IUCN say this frog is in very big danger of dying out. People put bad chemicals into the water, mostly from farms. Human beings cut down many trees near the frog's home and planted trees from other parts of the world, eucalyptus and needle trees. There are fish from far away in the lakes where the frogs lived, trout and carp, which can eat the frog. Visitors can also hurt this frog. Scientists found the dangerous fungus Batrachocytrium dendrobatidis on this frog. They think many frogs died of the dangerous disease chytridiomycosis before 2004, but they do not think it still kills many of these frogs.

The Espeletia marsupial frog, north shore marsupial frog, rana marsupial de La Cocha, or rana marsupial de Espeletia (Gastrotheca espeletia) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador and Colombia. The adult male frog is about 47.0–52.6 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog 44.3–51.9 mm. The frog can be different colors. It can be dark brown with lighter brown marks or green with brown or darker green marks. There is light green color where the four legs meet the body. The sides of the body have some blue-green color or they are green with some yellow color. The belly is yellow or green in color with some gray marks. The iris of the eye is brown in color. This frog lives in forests and paramo grassy places. People see this frog on plants. Scientists have seen the frog between 2530 and above sea level. Scientists have seen this frog in one protected place: Reserva Ecologica El Angel. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as swimming tadpoles, not froglets. Scientists from the IUCN say this frog is in danger of dying out. Human beings cut down too many trees to get wood to use, make places for people to live, and make farms, for example potato farms, and places to raise animals, for example cows and trout fish. Fires can also kill these frogs.

The Cordillera Colan marsupial frog (Gastrotheca abdita) is a frog. It lives in Peru. The adult male frog can be as big as 35 mm from nose to rear end and the adult female frog 46.2 mm. The skin of the frog's back is brown in color. This frog lives in Cordillera de Colán, higher up in the mountains where no trees grow. People see them in grassy places, bogs, and on bromeliad plants. Scientists have seen the frog between 2970 and above sea level. Scientists think this frog might live in one protected place: Santuario Nacional Cordillera de Colán. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young come out as small froglets, not swimming tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say they do not know if the frog is in danger of dying out. The frog's home, Cordillera de Colán, is far from where human beings live and work. Scientists think the frogs might be in danger from farms, but they are not sure.

La Siberia Marsupial Frog (Gastrotheca piperata) is a frog. It lives in Bolivia. This frog lives in trees in cloud forests on mountains. Scientists have seen the frog between 1850 m and 2800 m above sea level. There is a protected place where the frog lives, Parque Nacional Carrasco. Scientists used to think this was the same frog as Hyla splendens, but they changed their minds in 1992. Scientists think the female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back, like other frogs in Gastrotheca. Scientists from the IUCN say they do not know if this frog is in danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frogs live to make farms and places to raise animals.

Elicio's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca elicioi) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador and Peru. The adult male frog can be 46.4–67.8 mm long from nose to rear end and one adult female frog was 67.5 mm. The skin of the frog's back is dark brown in color and the sides of the body are bronze-brown in color with some yellow. The tops of the legs have some olive-green color. There is a bronze line from the mouth to where the front legs meet the body. There is a broken line down each side of the body. Some pareas are pale green in color with black or white spots. The belly is brown-gray in color with black or white marks. The throat is dark gray in color. The iris of the eye is copper in color with tiny black lines. Scientists named this frog for Elicio E. Tapia, an Ecuadorean biologist who helped collect many living things for museums in Ecuador. Scientists saw the frog between 2010 m and 2914 m above sea level in Ecuador's Loja Province, in tiny pieces of forest. Scientists first saw the frog near the entrance to Parque Nacional Podocarpus. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. The young emerge as tadpoles.

El Tambo marsupial frog (Gastrotheca lateonota) is a frog. It lives in Peru and Ecuador. The adult male frog is 54.8–61.4 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 54.0–63.7 mm. The skin of the frog's back is bright green in color. Next to the frog's backbone, it has green marks with brown or dark brown in them next. There are cream or bronze marks on the sides of the back. The sides of the body are brown in color with some green and more brown. The places where the four legs meet the body and the backs of the muscles are darker. The feet have blue color with black marks. The toes are dark bronze in color and sometimes have black marks. The belly is gray-brown in color with gray or brown marks. The iris of the eye is deep bronze in color with small black lines. Scientists use the dark marks on the frog's head to tell it apart from Gastrotheca monticola. Scientists gave this frog the Latin name lateonota because it means dark because of the dark marks on the frog's head. This frog lives in trees and on the ground in cloud forests. Scientists have seen the frog between 1020 and above sea level. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She carries the tadpoles to water, where they swim and grow. Scientists from the IUCN say this frog is in some danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frog lives by cutting down trees.

A gate is a place between two parts of a wall, or a fence which could be opened and closed to let people go through it. In the Middle Ages, a city gate also allowed people to go into a (walled) city. Nowadays, people also talk about gates at airports. When going on an aircraft, people need to get together in a certain area of the airport first. They then pass through some kind of doorway to get onto the plane. That is what is called gate.

The pouched frog or giant marsupial frog (Gastrotheca ovifera) is a frog. It lives in Venezuela. This frog is awake at night. It lives in low places and in forests on mountains and in lower places, for example Rancho Grande forest. Scientists have seen the frog between 890 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places: El Ávila National Park, San Esteban National Park, Yurubí National Park, and Henri Pittier National Park. The eggs hatch into small froglets, not swimming tadpoles. Scientists from the IUCN say the frogs are in some danger of dying out. People change the places where the frogs live to make farms, get wood to use, and make other things that people need and use. Scientists think the disease chytridiomycosis might also hurt this frog.

The mountain marsupial frog or Schmidt's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca splendens) is a frog. It lives in Peru. This frog lives in cloud forests. Scientists have seen the frog between 1900 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in Parque Nacional Amboró. Scientists from the IUCN say they are not sure if the frog is in danger of dying out. In some places, human beings change the places where the frogs live to make farms, make places for animals to live, make places to live, and make other things people need. The fungual disease chytridiomycosis could also hurt this frog.

The tortoise marsupial frog, Espada's marsupial frog, or rana marsupial tortuga (Gastrotheca testudinea) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador and Peru. The adult male frog is 49.8–61.1 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 56.8–82.6 mm. This frog can be different colors. Scientists have seen frogs with brown backs with green and dark brown marks and light-colored chests and bellies. They have seen frogs with green backs and orange or bronze bellies and bronze eyes with brown-pink lines. One young frog had an olive-brown back, red spots, green color under its eyes, a light gray belly, and bronze eyes with black lines. This frog lives in trees in cloud forests. Scientists have seen it at night on leaves and stems of trees and smaller plants. During they day, they see it in bromeliad plants. Scientists only found the frog in and near forests that were never cut down. Scientists have seen the frog between 700 andabove sea level. Scientists saw the frogs in some protected places: Pilon Lajas National Park, Carrasco National Park, Parque Nacional y Área Natural de Manejo Integrado Cotapata, and Parque Nacional del Manu. There are protected places where the frogs live: Parque Nacional Sumaco Napo-Galeras, Reserva Ecológica Antisana, Reserva Biológa San Francisco, Parque Nacional Llanganates, Parque Nacional Sangay. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small frog and is never a tadpole. Scientists have seen female frogs carrying 30-69 eggs at a time. Scientists in Ecuador say the frog is in some danger of dying out and scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. In some places, human beings change the places where the frogs live to make farms, make places for animals to live, and get wood to use. The fungual disease chytridiomycosis could also hurt this frog. The Museum of Zoology of the Pontificia Universidad Católica del Ecuador has some of these frogs living there.

The silver marsupial frog, plumbeous marsupial frog, or rana marsupial de plumbea (Gastrotheca plumbea) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador. The adult make frog is 42.1–61.0 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is 58.2–73.0 mm. The skin of the frog's back is green in color with or without marks. The throat can be light green or yellow-brown in color. There is brown color on the legs with bronze marks. The feet are green or brown in color. The belly is broze or brown or yellow-green during the day and cream-white at night. Where the legs meet the body, thre is bronze and blue or green and blue color during the day and blue by itself at night. The iris of the eye is light olive-green in color. Scientists gave the frog the Latin name plumbeus, for the metal lead, because the sample frog, which was dead and in liquid, was lead-gray in color. This frog lives in trees and is awake at night. It lives in cloud forests but people sometimes see it in forests that were cut down and are growing back. Scientists have seen the frog between 1300 andabove sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places: Reserva Ecológica Los Ilinizas, Reserva Ecológica Cotacachi-Cayapas, Estación Científica Río Guajalito, Bosque Protector Mindo-Nambillo, and Bosque Protector Cashca Totoras. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. Scientists have seen 20 to 28 eggs on one female at a time. After 8-10 months, the small frogs climb out of the pouch. This frog never swims as a tadpole. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in some danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frog lives to make farms, get wood to use, and make places to raise cows.

Weinland's marsupial frog or rana marsupial de Weinland (Gastrotheca weinlandii) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador, Peru, and Colombia. The adult male frog is 63.0 to 85.7 mm long from nose to rear end. The adult female frog is 68.4 to 86.0 mm. The frogs in this species can be different colors. The frogs that live in Sucumbíos are brown with olive-brown marks and yellow color on their sides. These frogs have light yellow color on their mouths. The sides of the head are olive-green. The throat and belly are white or cream in color. The iris of the eye is pink-bronze in color with brown lines. The frogs that live in Napo are brown in color with darker brown or gray-brown marks. The head is dark brown in color. The sides are dark brown with cream-brown marks. The bottoms of the feet are blue in color with brown marks. The belly is lighter in color with brown marks. The iris of the eye is dark in color. Frogs that live in Morona Santiago are gray-green in color with brown marks. The belly is a mix of brown and green. The bottoms of the feet are brown in color. The head is yellow-green in color. The iris of the eye has brown lines in it. The young frogs are green with olive-brown color. The head has brown marks. The belly is see-through yellow-green. The iris of the eye is bronze in color with black marks. This frog lives high in trees and is awake at night. It lives in cloud forests high in the mountains. Scientists have seen the frog between 1100 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frogs in some protected places: Parque Nacional Sumaco Napo-Galeras, Reserva Ecológica Antisana, Parque Nacional Llanganates, Parque Nacional Sangay, and Parque Nacional Natural Alto Fragua-Indiwasi. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. This frog hatches into a small froglet, not a tadpole. Even when the animal is still in its egg, it does not look like a tadpole. For example, many species of frog have keratin in their mouths like tadpoles do before they hatch out of their eggs, but G. cornuta does not. This frog has the biggest eggs of any amphibian. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. Human beings change the places where the frog lives to make farms, make places for cows to eat grass, get wood to use, and make places for people to live.

The Peru marsupial frog (Gastrotheca peruana) is a frog. It lives in Peru, in valleys in the Andes Mountains. This frog lives high in the mountains. It lives in grassy places, puna, and on farms. People see it under rocks and on plants near ponds. People have also seen this frog in towns. Scientists have seen the frog between 2300 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in one protected place, Parque Nacional de Huascaran. They think it could also live in Huayllay National Sanctuary, Junín National Reserve, and Chacamarca Historical Sanctuary. This frog has young in ditches, ponds that are there all year, ponds that dry up for part of the year, and other water that does not move. Frogs that live higher than 3000 m above sea level hatch out of their eggs into small froglets. Eggs lower than 2300 m above sea level hatch out of their eggs as swimming tadpoles. In between, they hatch into tadpoles that have legs. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is not in danger of dying out. Scientists think the frog could be in some danger when people dig in the ground for good rocks. People sometimes sell this frog as a pet, but scientists don't think that puts the frog in danger of dting out.

The Gualataco marsupial frog, Riobamba marsupial frog, Riobamba pouched frog, or rana marsupial Gualataco (Gastrotheca riobambae) is a frog. It lives in Ecuador. The adult male frog is about 34.1 – 56.8 mm long from nose to rear end and the adult female frog is about 48.6 – 66.4 mm. This frog lives on plants in forests on mountains. It can live in the forest, in grassy places, cornfields, city parks, and in dry, rocky places. Scientists have seen the frog between 1578 and above sea level. Scientists have seen the frog in protected places: Reserva Ecológica Los Ilinizas, Reserva Ecológica Cotacachi-Cayapas, Parque Nacional Cotopaxi, Refugio de Vida Silvestre Pasochoa, and Reserva de Producción Faunística Chimborazo. The female frog carries her eggs in a bag of skin on her back. She puts the tadpoles in small pools of water and in streams with still places. Inside the pouch, each tadpole grows bell gills. Scientists think that the bell gills help the mother frog give water and gas to the tadpoles, maybe food chemicals too. When the tadpole first comes out of their mother's body, it is 18 - 20 mm long, with the tail. Then the bell gills go back into the tadpole's body, and it grows new gills. The tadpole takes 41 days to one year to become a frog. People sometimes keep this frog as a pet. Scientists use this frog in experiments. Scientists from the IUCN say the frog is in some danger of dying out. People change the places where the frog lives to make towns, farms, and tree farms, for example for pine and eucalyptus trees. Bad chemicals and climate change could also hurt this frog. Scientists also found the dangerous fungus Batrachocytrium dendrobatidis on frogs and tadpoles.

Niceforo's marsupial frog (Gastrotheca nicefori) is a frog. It lives in Colombia, Venezuela, and Panama. This frog is nocturnal and lives in trees. It mostly lives in cloud forests, but people have also seen it in dry forests. It lives in shrubs and trees with other plants growing on them. Scientists have seen the frog between 400 and above sea level.
